title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: Hold for a licensing correction: Microsoft already requires an active Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to access Cowork, independently of whether this skill ships as a plugin. The roadmap facts and documented control paths and commands are supported; details specific to the planned model-app-builder skill remain unconfirmed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The required licence for using this skill is unpublished, with Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing stated only for the unconfirmed plugin delivery case.
claims.quote:
Before you begin, make sure you have:
- Microsoft Copilot access: An active Microsoft 365 Copilot license assigned to your account.
claims.fix: Replace the opening of Cost and licensing with: 'Cowork requires an active Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and enabled usage-based billing. Microsoft has not published an additional licence requirement or a credit rate specific to the model-app-builder skill.' Replace licensing.notes with: 'Cowork requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and is metered in Copilot Credits through usage-based billing. Any additional licence requirement or credit rate specific to this skill is not yet published.' The existing cited Get started with Copilot Cowork page states the general licence prerequisite regardless of plugin delivery.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A spending policy that selects Cowork grants Cowork access to its scoped users.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting a low credit limit does not block access to Cowork.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is. A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access.

claims.claim: A Cowork-selecting spending policy can be scoped to a security group.
claims.quote:
On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group.
On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.

claims.claim: Removing a user from every spending policy that selects Cowork removes access.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.claim: Configuration of the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents has no effect on who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Credit limits are not a real-time access gate, so users may start tasks after reaching a limit.
claims.quote: Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.

claims.claim: Managing Cowork plugins requires a tenant administrator or the Copilot administrator role.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center access: You must be a tenant administrator, or have the Copilot administrator role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users of Cowork plugins must have Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses: Users who use Cowork plugins must have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses assigned.

claims.claim: The System Administrator role provides the required role-assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: Dataverse database capacity covers table rows, metadata and relational data created by custom model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Tracks structured data stored directly in Dataverse, including table rows, metadata, and relational data created by Power Apps, Power Automate, Dynamics 365 customer engagement apps (Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Service, Dynamics 365 Marketing), and custom model-driven apps.

claims.claim: Capacity reporting excludes trial, preview, support and developer environments.
claims.quote: The capacity report counts default, production, and sandbox environments for consumption. It doesn't count trial, preview, support, and developer environments.

claims.claim: The spending-policy creation path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration and select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta supports POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies to create a spending policy.
claims.quote:
APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.
Create spendingPolicy | POST /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies | Create a new spending policy.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table row 2; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A Cowork plugin can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Block.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Agents > Tools.
Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab.
Select Block: No users in your tenant can access the plugin.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking applies to new conversations, while conversations already using the plugin continue until they end.
claims.quote: Blocking takes effect for new conversations. Conversations already in progress that use the plugin continue until they end.

claims.claim: The Package Management API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The cited package-block operation supports delegated work-account permissions, not application permissions.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.
Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported.
Application | Not available. | Not available.

claims.claim: The cited package-block API is unavailable in US Government L4, US Government L5 (DOD) and China operated by 21Vianet.
claims.quote:
Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet
✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌

claims.claim: User security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote:
select Manage.
In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment from the list.
Select Settings.
Select Users + permissions, and then select Users.
On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment-id> --user <upn> --role "<role-name>" assigns a user to a Dataverse environment with the specified role.
claims.quote:
Assign a user to a target Dataverse environment with specified security role.
pac admin assign-user `
  --environment 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 `
  --user "user@company.com" `
  --role "Basic User"
